description: Small deterministic retrieval set for the educational transcript demo.

transcript.text: The lesson introduces supervised learning, where labeled examples teach a model to map inputs to known outputs.
Gradient descent reduces a loss function by updating model weights in the direction of the negative gradient.
The learning rate controls the size of each gradient descent step; a step that is too large can overshoot the minimum.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training examples and performs poorly on unseen validation data.
A convolutional neural network applies learned filters over small image regions to detect features such as edges.
Regularization discourages unnecessarily complex models; dropout randomly disables units during training.

questions.question: How does gradient descent lower the loss?
What happens if the learning rate step is too large?
Why does a model fail on validation examples after memorizing training data?
How do CNN filters process image regions?
What does dropout do during training?
